title: The role of common variants of ABCB1, CYP3A4, and CYP3A5 genes in lipid-lowering efficacy and safety of simvastatin treatment.
text_summary: 本文发表于Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics（2005，IF=6.3），前瞻性评估ABCB1、CYP3A4和CYP3A5常见变异与辛伐他汀降脂疗效及安全性的关系。116名高胆固醇血症患者接受辛伐他汀20 mg/日，99人完成6个月疗效随访，17人因不良反应未完成，其中15人出现肌痛。校正协变量后，ABCB1 1236T携带者的总胆固醇和LDL胆固醇下降幅度大于野生型纯合子，2677G>A/T及单倍型分析得到相似结果。1236T、2677非G和3435T等位基因以及T-非G-T单倍型在肌痛患者中频率较低，提示可能具有保护作用。CYP3A4 -392A>G和CYP3A5*3未与疗效或耐受性显著相关。结果支持ABCB1遗传多态性影响辛伐他汀个体化降脂反应和肌肉不良反应风险。
text:
The role of common variants ofABCB1,
CYP3A4, and CYP3A5genes in lipid-lowering
efficacy and safety of simvastatin treatment
Objective: Our objective was to investigate the interactions between common polymorphisms in ABCB1,
CYP3A4, and CYP3A5 genes and the lipid-lowering efficacy and safety of the 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl–
coenzyme A reductase inhibitor simvastatin.
Methods: One hundred sixteen hypercholesterolemic patients were prospectively screened by physical exami-
nation, medical history, and clinical laboratory evaluation and were included in this study. Subjects entering
the study were treated with 20 mg/d simvastatin. Plasma lipid and lipoprotein levels were measured before
treatment, after 2 months of treatment, and after 6 months of treatment. Ninety-nine patients completed the
6-month follow-up and were included in the association analysis for treatment efficacy. Seventeen subjects
who had adverse drug reactions (ADRs) to simvastatin (ADR group) could not complete the 6-month
follow-up and were included in the association analyses for safety. Myalgia was observed in 15 of 17 subjects
and was the only ADR included in the association analyses, but other common ADRs were also observed.
Myalgia was defined as proximal or diffuse muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, or both pain and weakness,
with normal or slightly increased serum creatine phosphokinase levels. ABCB1 (1236C>T, 2677G >A/T,
and 3435C >T), CYP3A4 (/H11546392A>G), and CYP3A5 (6986A>G) allele variants were determined by poly-
merase chain reaction and restriction mapping.
Results: After adjustment for covariates, carriers of the ABCB1 1236T variant allele had a greater reduction in
total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol with simvastatin treatment, as compared with homozy-
gotes with the wild-type allele (/H1154629.0% [95% confidence interval (CI),/H1154625.9 to /H1154632.5] versus/H1154624.2% [95% CI,
/H1154619.0 to /H1154629.3] [P /H11549.042] and /H1154639.6% [95% CI, /H1154635.8 to /H1154644.0] versus/H1154633.8% [95% CI, /H1154627.4 to /H1154640.2]
[P /H11549.042], respectively). Similar results were observed for the 2677G>A/T polymorphism and haplotype data.
The 1236T, 2677non-G, and 3435T alleles were less frequent in ADR cases than in the non-ADR group (P < .05
for all single-nucleotide polymorphisms). Haplotype analyses also demonstrated a reduction of the T–non-G–T
haplotype frequency (20%) in patients in whom myalgia developed during simvastatin treatment, as compared
with the non-ADR group (41.4%) ( P /H11549.03). No significant associations were observed between the CYP3A4
/H11546392A>G and CYP3A5*3 allele variants and the efficacy or tolerability of simvastatin.
Conclusions: Our data suggest an association of ABCB1 gene polymorphisms and the efficacy and safety of
simvastatin. (Clin Pharmacol Ther 2005;78:551-8.)

Cholesterol-lowering therapy is the central approach
in the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovas-
cular disease, the leading cause of death worldwide.
1,2
The 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl– coenzyme A (HMG-
CoA) reductase inhibitors (statins) are well established
as pharmacologic agents that improve the lipid proﬁle
of dyslipidemic patients. These drugs decrease choles-

terol synthesis by competitively inhibiting HMG-CoA
reductase, the enzyme responsible for catalyzing the
conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate, a precursor of
cholesterol.
1
In recent years intense research has been focused on
identifying environmental and genetic factors respon-
sible for the interindividual variation in the outcome of
HMG-CoA inhibitor therapy, including aspects of efﬁ-
cacy (lipid-lowering response and progression of car-
diovascular heart disease) and safety.
3,4
Simvastatin is the pharmacologically inactive lac-
tone form of simvastatin hydroxy acid.5 On the basis of
a combination of 4 different in vitro strategies, Pruek-
saritanont et al 6 demonstrated that cytochrome P450
(CYP) 3A was the major ( /H1135080%) enzyme subfamily
involved in simvastatin lactone and hydroxy acid forms
metabolism. Both CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 were capable
of catalyzing the formation of the main simvastatin
metabolites.
6
CYP3A constitutes the largest portion of CYP pro-
tein in the liver and small intestine and plays an im-
portant role in the metabolism of numerous substrates.
Interindividual variability in the expression of CYP3A
is very high (20- to 40-fold),
7 making members of this
subfamily of genes major candidates for pharmacoge-
netic investigations. CYP3A4*1B results from an A to
G transition in the 5 /H11032ﬂanking region, whereas
CYP3A5*3 is the most frequent and functionally im-
portant single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the
CYP3A5 gene and consists of a 6986A /H11022G transition
within intron 3 that creates an alternative splice site in
the pre–messenger ribonucleic acid.
7,8 The frequency
of the functional wild-type allele (A6986) is reported to
be 5% to 15% for white subjects and 45% to 73% for
black subjects.
8
In addition to phase I metabolism, several studies
have examined the interaction of statins with
P-glycoprotein (P-gp) (also called MDR1 [multidrug re-
sistance 1]), a potent adenosine triphosphate– dependent
efﬂux pump for a wide variety of lipophilic compounds.
Earlier investigations have characterized simvastatin as
a substrate/inhibitor of P-gp.
9,10 Recently, Chen et al 11
demonstrated that simvastatin hydroxy acid is a P-gp
substrate and that the lactone form inhibits P-gp–
mediated transport with more efﬁcacy than its corre-
sponding acid form.
Given that drug transporters and drug-metabolizing
enzymes are the 2 major biologic factors determining
the pharmacokinetics of drugs,
12,13 we hypothesized
that genetic differences in genes encoding these pro-
teins could contribute to the variable response of the
HMG-CoA inhibitor simvastatin. To test this hypothe-
sis, we performed a prospective pharmacogenetic in-
vestigation of common polymorphisms in CYP3A4,
CYP3A5, and ABCB1 (gene coding for P-gp) genes and
the lipid-lowering efﬁcacy and safety of 20 mg/d sim-
vastatin.
METHODS
Study population. One hundred forty-six hypercho-
lesterolemic patients of European ancestry were re-
cruited in Porto Alegre, Brazil. For this prospective
study, all patients were screened by physical examina-
tion, medical history, and clinical laboratory evaluation
and were invited to participate in this study. Exclusion
criteria included the following: triglyceride level of
4.52 mmol/L or greater, unstable or uncontrolled clin-
ically signiﬁcant disease, uncontrolled hypothyroidism
or diabetes, and impaired hepatic or renal function.
None of the patients were undergoing previous
cholesterol-lowering therapy with statins or other
drugs. Subjects entering the study were treated with 20
mg/d simvastatin (Zocor; Merck Sharp & Dohme, Sa˜o
Paulo, Brazil) for 6 months. Patients continued taking
other medications throughout the study with no change,
including calcium channel blockers, /H9252-blockers, diuret-
ics, and other antihypertensive therapy ( Table I ).
Plasma lipid and lipoprotein levels were measured at
baseline and throughout the study. The Ethics Commit-
tee of the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul
(Porto Alegre, Brazil) approved the study protocol. All
participants in the study gave written informed consent.
Ninety-nine patients completed the 6-month follow-up
and were included in the association analysis for treat-
ment efﬁcacy. Seventeen subjects had adverse drug
reactions (ADRs) (ADR group), whereas 30 were ex-
cluded because of low compliance with simvastatin
treatment or because they did not show up for biochem-
ical testing. The compliance assessment with treatment
was veriﬁed by tablet count monthly.
The adverse effects were assessed during clinical
follow-up. Decisions on inclusion and exclusion were
made without awareness of the genotypes. The appear-
ance of common ADRs (myalgia, constipation, ﬂatu-
lence, dyspepsia, nausea, abdominal pain, and elevated
hepatic transaminase levels) was evaluated.
14
The most common ADR was myalgia, which was
deﬁned as proximal or diffuse muscle pain, tenderness,
or weakness, or both pain and weakness, with normal or
slightly increased serum creatine phosphokinase (CPK)
levels.
14,15 The following criterion was used to deﬁne
cases with adverse reactions: association of myalgia
with simvastatin treatment, unrelated to other condi-
tions that may contribute independently to muscle

aches, such as arthritis, viral myalgia, exercise-induced
myalgia, and ﬁbromyalgia.
Biochemical analysis. Blood samples were col-
lected from subjects after 12 hours of fasting. Total
cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein (HDL) choles-
terol, triglyceride, and glucose levels were determined
by conventional enzymatic methods. Low-density li-
poprotein (LDL) cholesterol was calculated according
to Friedewald et al.
16 Other biochemical parameters,
such as liver function test and CPK test results, were
obtained before and throughout the treatment.
Deoxyribonucleic acid analysis. Genomic deoxyri-
bonucleic acid (DNA) was isolated from peripheral
blood leukocytes by standard procedures.17 CYP3A4*1B
(A/H11002392G) was ampliﬁed by use of the forward primer
5/H11032-GGAATGAGGACAGCCATAGAGACAACTGCA-3/H11032
and reverse primer 5 /H11032-CCTTTCAGCTCTGTGTTGC-
TCTTTGCTG-3/H11032. The sense primer was designed to
generate a PstI endonuclease restriction site when the
/H11002392G allele is incorporated. Ampliﬁcation reactions
of 25 /H9262L were performed by use of 0.2-mmol/L de-
oxyribonucleoside triphosphates, 2.0-mmol/L magne-
sium chloride, 0.4 /H9262mol/L of each primer, 100 ng of
genomic DNA, an d1Uo f Taq DNA polymerase
(Biotools, Madrid, Spain). Cycle conditions were 94°C
for 5 minutes, followed by 35 cycles of 94°C for 60
seconds, 60°C for 60 seconds, and 72°C for 60 seconds,
with a ﬁnal extension step of 5 minutes at 72°C. The
polymerase chain reaction products were digested with
1 0Uo f PstI and the fragments were separated by
electrophoresis on a 2.5% agarose gel.
ABCB1 (1236C/H11022T, 2677G /H11022A/T, and 3435C /H11022T)
and CYP3A5 (6986A/H11022Go r *3) were genotyped as
previously described.
18-20
Statistical analysis. Allele frequencies were esti-
mated by gene counting. Both deviation from Hardy-
Weinberg equilibrium and allelic distributions between
groups were assessed by chi-square tests or, when
appropriate, by Fisher exact test with the use of Graph-
Pad InStat software, version 2.04a (GraphPad Soft-
ware, San Diego, Calif). Haplotype frequencies and
linkage disequilibrium were estimated by use of the
Multiple Locus Haplotype Analysis program (version
2.0)
21 and Arlequin software (version 2.000),22 respec-
tively. D max (theoretic maximum linkage disequilib -
rium [D]) and D /H11032(the relative magnitude of D as
compared with its theoretic maximum, calculated as
D/D
max) values were calculated as described by Le -
wontin.23 Continuous variables were expressed as mean
/H11006SD. Triglyceride levels were log-transformed before
analysis because of their skewed distribution, but non-
transformed values are presented in the Results section.
To determine the association of the genotypes with
response to simvastatin treatment, mean changes in
plasma lipid levels among genotypes were compared by
a general linear model by use of the type III sum of
squares. This sum of squares applies to unbalanced
study designs and quantiﬁes the effect of an indepen-
dent variable after adjustment for all other variables
included in the model. Age, sex, smoking status, hy-
pertension, prior cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and
baseline lipid levels were included in each model as
covariates.
RESULTS
Characteristics of study population. Demographic
and key clinical characteristics are shown in Table I .
Patients who completed the 6-month follow-up were
aged between 25 and 82 years (59.2 /H1100610.7 years), and
25.3% were men. Patients continued taking other med-
ications throughout the study with no change, including
calcium channel blockers (10.1%), /H9252-blockers (23.2%),
diuretics (26.3%), and other antihypertensive therapy
(22.2%).

after 2 months of treatment. These patients did not

ing ADRs were observed: myalgia (n /H110057), myalgia
plus abdominal pain (n /H110051), myalgia with increased

range (n /H110057), abdominal pain (n /H110051), and allergic

was deﬁned as 174 U/L for men and 140 U/L for
women. No signiﬁcant myopathy or rhabdomyolysis
was observed in this small short-term study. Patients
who completed the 6-month follow-up had mean base-

18-101 U/L) and 58.8 /H110065.5 U/L (range, 19-130 U/L),

Treatment with 20 mg/d simvastatin signiﬁcantly
reduced the plasma levels of total cholesterol (/H1100227.8%,
P /H11021.0001) and LDL cholesterol (/H1100238.2%, P /H11021.0001).
Triglyceride levels were modestly reduced (/H1100210.5%, P
/H11005.08), whereas the increase in HDL cholesterol did not
reach statistical signiﬁcance ( /H110010.8%, P /H11005.75). There
were no signiﬁcant differences in baseline levels of
total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, and LDL cholesterol
between the ADR group and patients who completed
the 6-month follow-up. The baseline triglyceride levels
were greater in patients in whom ADRs developed
compared with patients who completed the follow-up
(2.16 versus 1.67, P /H11005.01) (Table II).
Association between ABCB1, CYP3A4, and CYP3A5
gene polymorphisms and cholesterol-lowering ther-
apy. The genotype distributions for each polymorphism
did not show statistically signiﬁcant differences com-
pared with those expected with Hardy-Weinberg equi-
librium (data not shown). The mean percent reductions
in lipid and lipoprotein levels according to genotypes
are shown in Table III. After adjustment for covariates,
carriers of the ABCB1 1236T variant allele had a
greater reduction of total cholesterol and LDL choles-
terol with simvastatin treatment, as compared with ho-
mozygotes with the wild-type allele ( /H1100229.0% versus
/H1100224.2% [P /H11005.042] and /H1100239.6% versus /H1100233.8% [P /H11005
.042], respectively). Similar results were observed for
the 2677G/H11022A/T polymorphism. The mean percentage
decrease in plasma total cholesterol and LDL choles-
terol was greater in carriers of the 2677A/T allele
compared with subjects homozygous for the 2677G
allele ( /H1100229.2% versus /H1100223.7% [ P /H11005.026] and
/H1100239.7% versus /H1100233.8% [P /H11005.05], respectively).
We also evaluated the effect of ABCB1 haplotypes
on total cholesterol and LDL cholesterol responses to
simvastatin treatment, grouping subjects as T–non-G–T
haplotype carriers (n /H1100563) versus noncarriers (n /H1100534)
of this haplotype. This comparison showed signiﬁcant
differences in lipid-lowering efﬁcacy for total choles-
terol and LDL cholesterol. The reductions in T–non-
G–T carriers for both variables were greater than those
observed for noncarriers ( /H1100229.7% versus /H1100223.6% for
total cholesterol [ P /H11005.012] and /H1100240.1% versus
/H1100233.9% for LDL cholesterol [ P /H11005.036]).
No signiﬁcant associations were observed between
the CYP3A4 /H11002392A/H11022G and CYP3A5 6986A/H11022G allele
variants and the efﬁcacy of simvastatin (data not
shown). Because CYP3A4 expression is known to be
affected by many coadministered drugs that are
CYP3A4 substrates, inhibitors, or inducers,
24,25 data
for association of /H11002392A/H11022G polymorphism were re-
analyzed excluding patients taking CYP3A4 substrates,
inhibitors, or inducers. Again, no association was dis-
closed between CYP3A4 gene polymorphism and
changes in lipid and lipoprotein levels after treatment in
this subsample (data not shown).

served for ABCB1 polymorphisms between subjects
with myalgia as an ADR (ADR group, n /H1100515) and
those without ADRs (non-ADR group, n /H1100599) (Table
IV). Among subjects in the ADR group, no homozy-
gotes for the alleles 1236T, 2677non-G, and 3435T
were observed. Genotype frequencies of the 3435C /H11022T
polymorphism differed statistically between the ADR
and non-ADR groups ( P /H11005.04). When allele frequen-
cies were compared, the 1236T, 2677non-G, and 3435T
alleles were less frequent in subjects with myalgia than
in the non-ADR group ( P /H11021.05 for all SNPs). No
differences in allele frequencies at the CYP3A4 and
CYP3A5 polymorphisms were observed between the
ADR group and non-ADR group.
Haplotype frequencies for all 3 ABCB1 (MDR1)
gene polymorphisms were estimated by use of a max-
imum likelihood method ( Table V). As a result of the
strong linkage disequilibrium (D /H11032/H110220.82, P /H11005.0001),
4 haplotypes accounted for 94.9% of the genetic vari-
ability related to the 3 investigated ABCB1 polymor-
phisms. In the non-ADR group the most frequent hap-
lotypes were T/non-G/T (41.4%), C/G/C (41%), C/G/T
(8.1%), and C/non-G/T (3.5%), whereas in the ADR
group they were C/G/C (60%), T/non-G/T (20%), and
C/G/T (10%). When the haplotype distributions were
compared (haplotype T/non-G/T versus other haplo-
types), statistical analyses demonstrated a reduction of
the 1236T/2677non-G/3435T haplotype frequency
(20%) in patients in whom myalgia developed during
simvastatin treatment, as compared with the non-ADR
group (41.4%) ( P /H11005.027). This ﬁnding seems to sug-
gest an association between ABCB1 gene variants and
an increased susceptibility for development of myalgia.
Therefore ABCB1 could be considered a novel factor
that could be related to the success rate of simvastatin
treatment. There were no signiﬁcant differences in sex,
age, body mass index, and concomitant therapies be-
tween the ADR group and patients who completed the
6-month follow-up ( Table I).
DISCUSSION
In this prospective study we examined the possible
inﬂuence of common polymorphisms in ABCB1,
CYP3A4, and CYP3A5 genes and the efﬁcacy and
safety of treatment with 20 mg simvastatin. Our major
ﬁndings were the association of ABCB1 gene variants
and haplotypes with both the efﬁcacy and the safety of
simvastatin treatment.
P-gp is a member of the adenosine triphosphate–
binding cassette family and is encoded by the human
ABCB1 gene (adenosine triphosphate– binding cas-
sette, subfamily B1), also called MDR1. This protein
function as a cellular efﬂux pump to control the intra-
cellular concentration of potentially harmful substances

and thereby prevents accumulation of such compounds

13,26
The role of ABCB1 gene polymorphisms on statin
therapy was previously addressed by Kajinami et al. 27
They reported the effect of the 2677G /H11022A/T and
3435C/H11022T polymorphisms on hypolipidemic response
to atorvastatin treatment. In that investigation they
found that the absolute and percentage changes in LDL
cholesterol in variant allele carriers (3435T) were sig-
niﬁcantly larger than those in homozygotes for the
wild-type allele (3435C) in a gender-speciﬁc manner,
showing signiﬁcant effects only in the female group.
They also evaluated the effect of haplotypes
(2677G/H11022A/T/H110023435C/H11022T) on atorvastatin treatment. In
female non-G–T haplotype carriers LDL improvement
was greater than in carriers of other haplotypes. Despite
the use of a nonstratiﬁed statistical analysis, our sample
is mainly constituted by women (74.7%); therefore
both single-polymorphism and haplotype data pre-
sented herein are in the same direction as those previ-
ously reported by Kajinami et al.
Large clinical trials have demonstrated that statins
are well tolerated and severe adverse effects rarely
develop in patients.
1,2 However, recently, strategies to
improve the therapeutic proﬁle of statins that include
optimization of safety through a pharmacogenetic ap-
proach have been proclaimed as a step toward person-
alized medicine.
28 The most common ADRs for statins
as a class of drugs are gastrointestinal disturbance,
elevated hepatic transaminase levels, and skeletal mus-

cle abnormalities.14,29 Muscular adverse reactions have
been reported for commercially available statins with
an incidence of 6.2% to 9.1% for myalgia and 0.1% to
1.8% for myopathy.
15 The precise mechanism of statin-
induced muscle disorders is unknown, but some risk
factors for this reaction include treatment with high
doses of statins, advanced age, body weight and size,
impaired metabolism, or coadministration of CYP3A4
or P-gp substrates or inhibitors.
15 In our study we also
conducted an investigation to assess the relationship
between polymorphisms in the main genes involved in
simvastatin disposition and the occurrence of the statin-
associated adverse effect myalgia. Our results sug-
gested, despite its small sample size, that the ABCB1
variant alleles 1236T, 2677non-G, and 3435T and the
haplotype derived from these 3 SNPs were less frequent
in subjects with myalgia than in subjects with no ad-
verse effect. Our study has limitations that require
consideration. First, in this preliminary investigation
the sample size of patients in whom myalgia developed
was quite small; thus these data require independent
conﬁrmation in a larger sample cohort. Second, we
cannot exclude the possibility that statin-associated ad-
verse effects will develop with a longer treatment pe-
riod or higher doses of simvastatin in patients included
in the non-ADR group. Third, patients in whom myal-
gia develops are taking comedications that are CYP3A4
or MDR1 substrates and inhibitors, and therefore the
observed results might be a result of confounder vari-
ables. However, despite these limitations, our results
should be viewed as hypothesis-raising; clearly, more
investigations are warranted because no other study has
addressed this speciﬁc issue about the relationship be-
tween these SNPs and the simvastatin-associated ad-
verse effects.
In this study we also investigated the association of
the most common variants in CYP3A4 (CYP3A4*1B)
and CYP3A5 (CYP3A5*3) with the safety and efﬁcacy
of simvastatin treatment. Recent observations in pa-
tients treated with 10 mg atorvastatin demonstrated that
homozygotes for the CYP3A4*1B (/H11002392G) allele had
signiﬁcantly higher posttreatment LDL cholesterol lev-
els than did subjects who were carriers of the /H11002392A
allele, but no differences in absolute and percent
change in LDL cholesterol were found.
30 A recent
study with 46 subjects taking statins that undergo
CYP3A-mediated biotransformation (lovastatin, simva-
statin, and atorvastatin) showed that the lipid-lowering
response was smaller in CYP3A5 expressors than in
nonexpressors.
31 The mean serum LDL concentration
in subjects possessing the CYP3A5*1 allele was 24%
higher than in subjects homozygous for the CYP3A5*3
allele. Our results did not replicate those previous ﬁnd-
ings in which CYP3A4 /H11002392A/H11022G and CYP3A5*3
polymorphisms were associated with treatment efﬁ-
cacy. The lack of association between lipid response to
simvastatin and CYP3A4 genotypes may result, in part,
from sample size, because no /H11002392G homozygote was
observed in our investigation. However, the sample
investigated for CYP3A5 polymorphism is smaller than
that investigated here. Moreover, differences in the
study designs (dose, treatment duration) and differ-
ences in the relative contributions of CYP3A protein in
the metabolism of different statins might inﬂuence the
observation of conﬂicting results.
In summary, the data presented here provide further
evidence for the association of ABCB1 gene variation
and the efﬁcacy of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor treat-
ment. This study also observed a relationship between
the ABCB1 genotypes and the occurrence of simvasta-
tin myalgia. To our knowledge, this is the ﬁrst study
describing an association between this genetic variation
and the safety of simvastatin treatment; therefore addi-
tional studies will be needed to conﬁrm whether
ABCB1 polymorphisms are associated with the suscep-
tibility to adverse effects during simvastatin treatment.

image_summary: 第1页：Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics研究首页，包含题名、作者和结构式摘要；概述116名患者接受辛伐他汀后ABCB1、CYP3A4和CYP3A5变异与疗效及肌痛风险的关联。
第2页：介绍辛伐他汀代谢与转运的药物遗传学背景，并详述研究设计、受试者、20 mg/日治疗方案、随访和不良反应判定。
第3页：说明血脂、生化指标、DNA提取、PCR与限制性酶切分型和统计方法，进入疗效与不良反应结果并列出基线特征。
第4页：表格比较完成与未完成研究者及ABCB1基因型的血脂变化，报告1236T和2677非G等位基因与更大降脂幅度的关系。
第5页：继续展示基因型与疗效及肌痛的关联表，进入讨论，分析ABCB1变异对辛伐他汀转运、暴露和不良反应的潜在影响。
第6页：列出单倍型及双倍型频率与疗效、安全性的关系，讨论CYP3A4/CYP3A5未见显著关联及样本量限制。
第7页：完成讨论与结论，评价ABCB1药物转运、他汀肌肉不良反应和个体化治疗意义，并开始参考文献。
第8页：参考文献续页，列出辛伐他汀药代动力学、ABCB1与CYP3A遗传变异、降脂疗效和肌病风险相关研究。
